Tauri transport: reach the Jolt daemon through a desktop shell's Rust
commands instead of direct HTTP, so the webview never needs network access
to the daemon.

The host application must expose these Tauri commands (the contract Spoke
established):

```rust
#[tauri::command]
async fn daemon_request(base_path: String, path: String, method: String,
                        body: Option<Value>, session_token: Option<String>)
                        -> Result<Value, String>;
#[tauri::command]
async fn daemon_publish_bytes(session_token: String, path: String,
                              bytes: Vec<u8>, file_name: String,
                              mime_type: String) -> Result<Value, String>;
#[tauri::command]
async fn daemon_append(session_token: String, path: String, bytes: Vec<u8>,
                       file_name: String, mime_type: String)
                       -> Result<Value, String>;
```
See the app development guide for the full Rust implementation to copy.

readme.text:
# jolt-sdk

TypeScript SDK for building applications on the [Jolt](https://github.com/alexanderwanyoike/jolt) network.

Jolt applications do not own accounts. They ask the local Jolt daemon for a
capability-scoped session that the user approves in Jolt Console, then publish
signed content under the user's identity, read other identities' content, and
exchange encrypted objects through recipient-controlled ingress. This SDK is
the typed client for that contract, extracted from the seam proven in
[Spoke](https://github.com/alexanderwanyoike/spoke) and
[Pastey](https://github.com/alexanderwanyoike/pastey).

## Install

## Quick start

projection. Failures from publishes and sends throw

## Documentation

Full API reference is generated from the TSDoc comments with

(typedoc) and published on the
[Jolt website](https://alexanderwanyoike.github.io/jolt/sdk/). The app
development guide walks through building a small social app with Tauri.

## Development

```sh
yarn install
yarn test        # vitest
yarn typecheck
yarn build       # emits dist/
yarn docs        # emits docs/api.json + docs-html/
```
